title: docs(lint): dashboard-filter-binding-unknown explanation counts a globalFilters entry named dateRange as declared
body:

_Requested by **Warren** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8?thread=cmsg_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8UFVez1aipH3zDDpgxd3umQ)_
Fixes #29382

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:`os explain dashboard-filter-binding-unknown` 的一句说明,和 `validate-widget-bindings.ts` 里两段注释;规则代码不变,新增一个测试。
- 为什么改:旧说明称「没声明 `dateRange` 的仪表盘上,`dateRange` 绑定一律报错」;实测规则接受名为 `dateRange` 的 `globalFilters` 条目,说明与行为不符。
- 风险与回滚:只改说明文字与注释,行为零变化;回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`(第 407–410 行那句)、`packages/lint/src/validate-widget-bindings.test.ts`(新测试)。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run src/validate-widget-bindings.test.ts -t dashboard-filter-binding-unknown`,预期 13 个用例全绿。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

- `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`, rule `dashboard-filter-binding-unknown` only: the third paragraph said "A `dateRange` key on a dashboard that declares no `dateRange` is reported the same way". It now says a `dateRange` key is reported only when the dashboard declares neither `dateRange` nor a `globalFilters` entry named `dateRange`, because either one is a declared filter under that name.
- `packages/lint/src/validate-widget-bindings.ts`: the rule family docblock and the `DASHBOARD_FILTER_BINDING_UNKNOWN` docblock say the same. No code line changed.
- `packages/lint/src/validate-widget-bindings.test.ts`: one new case in the `dashboard-filter-binding-unknown` block. The dashboard has no `dateRange`, a `globalFilters` entry `{ name: 'dateRange', field: 'signed_at', type: 'date' }`, and a widget with `filterBindings: { dateRange: false }`. It expects zero findings.
- `.changeset/29382-filter-binding-daterange-prose.md`: a patch for `@objectstack/lint`, because the explanation text ships in its `dist/`.

## Why

The card asked for a measurement first. The rule takes its declared names from `dashboardFilterDefs`, which adds every `globalFilters` entry under its `name`. So a `globalFilters` entry named `dateRange` is declared even when the dashboard has no `dateRange`. The new test measured it on `origin/main` 94d3e254 before any prose edit: the case passed with zero findings. The rule accepts the binding, so this PR takes the prose-only arm and leaves the rule body alone. The runtime agrees: objectui `resolveDashboardFilterDefs` (`ui/packages/core/src/utils/dashboard-filters.ts`) builds the same name set.

## Tests

- Measurement, before any prose edit, tree 94d3e254 plus the new test only: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/validate-widget-bindings.test.ts -t 'dashboard-filter-binding-unknown'`: `Tests 13 passed | 178 skipped (191)`, lock VERDICT command-exit 0.
- Final head: see Verification.

## Acceptance notes

- `packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.zod.ts` still says `dateRange` is "reserved for the built-in dashboard date range" (the `globalFilters[].name` TSDoc) and "(dateRange only when declared)" (the `filterBindings` describe). Both are on the spec side that open PR #29370 owns, which keeps a `globalFilters` entry named `dateRange` accepted on a dashboard without `dateRange`. They are outside this card's file surface. carrier: PR #29370.
- The finding's hint for an undeclared `dateRange` key still reads "Declare `dateRange` on the dashboard, or delete the `dateRange` entry." It is reached only when neither declaration exists, so it is accurate; it does not mention the `globalFilters` spelling. Not changed, because the claim limits the rule body to the false-positive arm.
